title: About Long Island Nepalese Society - NY
paragraphs: Although Nepal is a small country in terms of geographical area, its social, cultural, and geographical diversity is remarkably broad. Nepal is known to the international community not only for Mount Everest and the birthplace of Lord Buddha, but also for its hardworking, friendly, multicultural, and honest citizens who have established a distinct identity in the international community.

Although Nepal established diplomatic relations with the United States in 1947, the arrival of Nepalis in the United States became more widespread from the late 1990s. In recent years, a growing number of Nepalis have been coming to the United States every year for higher education, diversity programs, permanent residency, business, and other opportunities, making the United States one of the most preferred destinations for Nepali immigrants.
New York City has also become one of the preferred destinations in the United States for a large number of Nepalis to live.

Long Island, a suburban area located close to New York City, is a very convenient and beautiful place to live. Close to New York City yet peaceful and scenic, with its proximity to the ocean, parks, excellent schools and universities, and many other attractions, Long Island has seen a growing Nepali population in both Nassau and Suffolk counties. By around 2010, approximately 200 Nepalis were living primarily in the areas of Hicksville and Levittown. With the desire to create opportunities for Nepalis living abroad to meet, build goodwill and brotherhood, celebrate festivals together, and support one another during difficult times, the Long Island Nepalese Society was established in 2010 through the initiative of several local community members. The organization was officially registered and began operating in 2012. Since then, it has become a well-known and respected social organization among the Nepali community locally, throughout New York, and across the United States. Today, approximately 5,000 Nepalis live in the area, with around 710 registered members.

Many Nepalis have recognized the importance of finding ways to fulfill our shared aspirations, exchange ideas, and expand opportunities for progress. More importantly, there is a need to build a common identity, move forward together, and unite in order to fulfill the aspirations we have inherited from our families and our country. The Long Island Nepalese Society has been serving as a bridge toward this goal. Through this organization, we can continue to exchange our ideas and concerns and help fellow Nepalis overcome their challenges. It is this spirit of unity, cooperation, and mutual support that continues to guide our community.
